(i) neighbourhood socio-economic status and screen time were associated with soft drink intake; (ii) proximity to grocery stores was associated with soft drink avoidance; (iii) screen time and socio-economic status were associated with fruit juice intake; (iv) proximity to grocery store was not associated with fruit juice consumption.

children of pre-school ages who lived within 2 km of a grocery stores and fast food restaurants were significantly less likely than those who did not to drink soft drinks during the past week, and those who participated in > 2 h of screen-time daily were significantly more likely than those who participated in <2 h of screen -time daily to drink soft drinks and exceed the recommended weekly servings of fruit juice.

neighbourhoods of low socio-economic status, and those with high availability of fast-food restaurants, were significantly associated with higher consumption of regular soft drinks among children of pre- school age.
